A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MAP research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–F. The readable equations, tables, figures and algorithms support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v4 reports original model-merging experiments in Tables 2–4 and additional medical-image, multilingual, ResNet, nested-merging and Bayesian MAP results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons and a math/code language-model merging experiment.

M1.justification: Quadratic surrogate fitting, sigmoid/softplus transformations, Pareto search, Bayesian sampling and nested merging remain unchanged. The expanded Section 3.3 primarily incorporates explanations already present in v4 Appendix E.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds mathematics and coding evaluation on GSM8k and HumanEval, identified in Figure 9. This substantially extends the language-model evaluation from multilingual generation to trade-offs between distinct specialist capabilities. Existing vision, medical and multilingual coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v5 adds MOEA/D, Ada-Merging++ and DELLA-Merging to the comparisons in Figure 5 and Table 4. These introduce a dedicated Pareto-search comparator and two additional merging methods across the existing two-to-eight-task evaluation. The earlier comparators remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce a MOEA/D configuration with population size 50 and 20 generations, and a Llama-2-13B math/code merging configuration. Existing coefficient budgets, win-rate calculations and the 20-preference-vector evaluation remain unchanged. These are added settings rather than evidence that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The task-vector norm analysis, GD/IGD sensitivity to evaluation budget, nested-merging comparisons, Bayesian sampling comparisons and illustrated failure case are retained. The added baseline and math/code evaluations do not introduce a separately reported ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same uncertainty-reporting practices and Algorithm 3 bootstrap settings. No changed seed counts, repeated-run procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests are documented. Table 4 changes standard-deviation values without describing a change in their estimation.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds three baseline result series across two to eight tasks; their eight-task means are 72.55 for Ada-Merging++, 71.49 for DELLA-Merging and 68.59 for MOEA/D. MAP's means remain unchanged, but its standard deviations change, including 72.96±0.73 to 72.96±2.52 for eight tasks. Appendix D.4 adds the math/code Pareto curve and distance results, including GD 0.039 and GD+IGD 0.057; its IGD entry is malformed in print.

T1.justification: The Pareto definitions, Assumption 1, quadratic derivation, closed-form regression results and Appendix C proofs are unchanged. Relocation of the motivating norm analysis does not alter the mathematical assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about low-compute Pareto-front estimation, broad applicability, Bayesian and nested variants, and compatibility with task-vector merging. The additional experiments support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds an interpretation of MOEA/D's solution diversity and evaluation cost relative to MAP. Appendix D.4 explains choosing Llama-2 specialists through shared configuration and identifies differing Qwen-2.5 RoPE settings as a merging obstacle. The earlier sparse multilingual-front and nested-merging limitations remain.

D1.justification: v5 provides checkpoint identifiers and access links for the new Llama-2, WizardMath and code-alpaca experiment, alongside MOEA/D population and generation settings. It does not supply a detailed math/code evaluation protocol. Existing code access and core implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds MOEA/D and DELLA references and expands Appendix B with WARM/WARP, evolutionary merging and Bayesian model-merging work. It also removes some earlier discussion and citations concerning robust fine-tuning, tangent-space task arithmetic and related motivation. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 copyedits numerous passages, updates author affiliations and publication headers, integrates the former Motivation subsection into Methods, and moves variant explanations from Appendix E into Section 3.3. These are localized reorganizations within the retained overall structure.

P2.justification: v5 adds the math/code Figure 9, expands Tables 4 and 7, and redraws the main comparison plots with additional comparator markers and legends. The discretization illustration moves from v4 Figure 5 to v5 Figure 11 in the appendix. Other figures are largely retained with renumbering, caption edits and layout shifts.

improvement.justification: MOEA/D supplies a more relevant test of Pareto-search efficiency than brute-force comparison alone, while GSM8k/HumanEval adds a clear specialist-capability trade-off beyond v4's sparse multilingual fronts. These strengthen the empirical support. The gain is limited by sparse new evaluation details, unexplained Table 4 standard-deviation revisions and the malformed new IGD entry in Table 7.
